Clean UI (almost bordering on a rip-off of Postman.. but I guess familiarity helps users get going faster). Lovely to see that things aren't held behind a Login button, ala Postman and Insomnia.

Only one workspace is available when offline. You can't point your Workspace data to a specific directory like bruno does. Self-hosting login is not possible in the desktop app. Cannot save specific responses like postman. Can't create documentation for a folder/request.
I just tried it. It feels like postman, very slow when typing json body. But it's small, and startup time is instant. I prefer bruno, but we do not talk about bruno.
I love hoppscotch and I'm a happy user of their PWA - not sure I understand the benefit that a framework like Tauri provides in addition?

Hoppscotch is a very cool product and now they also support the mTLS authentication, which was a long-awaited one. We moved out from Postman to use JMeter, since back then the feature was not available. Pretty happy to see it here again.

I believe both Bruno and Hoppscotch are 'open core' with expensive paid plans for additional/enterprise functionality, and they limit community-contributed functionality in the open source versions to avoid competing with the commercial versions.
Going to leave this here for shady practices. A pull request was declined by the CEO since they were planning to build an OIDC feature into the enterprise plan (referencing PR #3266).

Self-hosted magic link email sign-in fails with 500 Internal Server Error even after configuring MAILER_SMTP_URL correctly and testing with MailCatcher; backend logs show 'email/failed' error in AuthService.signInMagicLink.

Would be nice to sync storage over git. My team runs into this problem with Postman and any other web request UI - the web request collections are synced differently than our git repos. Why not make storage git-friendly, like Jupyter notebooks do.
Fun fact: this used to be named Postwoman as a play on Postman being a popular API client.
